A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. Relocated background, examples, and proofs can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original simulations comparing incentive-aware and incentive-unaware counterfactual estimation, including sensitivity studies averaged over 50 runs.

after.justification: Section 7 retains those original simulations and additionally reports an application of the asymptotic overlap test to simulated data.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the PCR estimator are retained. However, the asymptotic overlap test's decision threshold changes from 1-z_0.95 in v1 Section 5.2 to z_0.95 in v2 Section 6.2, modifying its decision rule.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic two-type, two-intervention panel setting. The added overlap diagnostic checks an assumption within this retained setting; no new dataset, population, domain, or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The simulations retain the same comparison: incentivized exploration versus an incentive-unaware ablation, both using Agarwal et al.'s adaptive PCR estimator. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: V2 adds a diagnostic evaluation using all type 0 units as donors and one type 1 unit as the test unit. The existing prediction experiments retain 500 alternating units, T0=T1=100, and the same noise distribution.

E4.justification: V2 Section 7 adds a diagnostic check showing whether the asymptotic test detects the deliberately constructed lack of overlap. The existing latent-dimension and belief-gap sensitivity studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The asymptotic significance cutoff is revised and its empirical application is first reported. The existing 50-run averages and one-standard-deviation bands remain unchanged. Calibration remains inconsistent: v2 defines z_0.95 as the 95th standard-normal quantile but reports it as approximately 1.96.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports an overlap-test statistic of approximately 2.24, compares it with a stated cutoff of 1.96, and concludes that overlap is absent. All eight prediction-error plot panels are identical: v1 Figures 1–2 become v2 Figures 2–3.

T1.justification: V1 Assumption 3.1(4) requires initial overlap for both types under their preferred interventions; v2 Assumption 4.1(4) requires it only for type 1 under treatment. The asymptotic cutoff also changes mathematically. The central theorems and appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit novelty claim about the connection between panel-data decision-making and noisy contextual bandits. The principal overlap-recovery and counterfactual-estimation claims remain. Synthetic interventions and both hypothesis tests, newly emphasized in the abstract, already existed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explains the relationship between horizontal and vertical regression and why both require overlap. It qualifies the at-most-r subtype argument with knowledge of which subpopulations overlap, and newly states applicability to any linear function of expected post-intervention outcomes.

D1.justification: V2 refines the simulation recipe by correcting inconsistent zero-based indexing and explicitly specifying r/2-component nonzero blocks. These are limited documentation corrections; the identical plots do not establish that the simulations were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds works by Agarwal et al. on error-in-variable regression, Hu et al. on combinatorial exploration, Ngo et al. on algorithmic instruments, and Shen et al. on horizontal/vertical regression. It expands the latter relationship and withdraws the explicit bandit-connection novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. V2 separates Model and Preliminaries, moves the overlap-necessity theorem before the exploration algorithm, relocates detailed PCR background to Appendix A, and moves Example 3.3 to Example B.5. Explanatory passages are expanded throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adds a boxed interaction-protocol Figure 1 and compacts and repositions the algorithm displays. The existing result figures retain their panels, axes, legends, and plotted content, with renumbering and surrounding text reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 improves accessibility through clearer organization and explanations of regression choices and applicability, while retaining technical material in the appendices. The new diagnostic provides limited additional evidence, and the threshold revision partly repairs v1's test. However, the remaining quantile/calibration inconsistency limits that gain; the core algorithms, proofs, and plotted results are largely unchanged.
